observations: Three eye-like forms occupy the head: a small tilted diamond high on the forehead, a broad blue oval below left and a rounded blue frame below right.
A dark horizontal mouth is crossed by closely spaced black vertical bars and white tooth-like marks, above a small outlined chin form.
Yellow and orange marks cover the crown, while teal, lavender and magenta lines surround the head and cross its outline.
reading: The three eye-like forms offer different ways into the face: a small diamond high on the forehead, a broad oval and a tightly ringed lower eye. Their uneven placement can read as startled or unsteady. Vertical bars across the mouth make the expression harder to settle. Warm yellows and oranges gather above while cool teal surrounds the head, keeping that unsettled gaze in a bright field.
contextAngle: "Wobbler" sits near the end of the owned scrimshaw works by recorded creation, between "Scrimshaw 40" and "Scrimshaw 41." Its face-forward composition and dense line layering connect it visually to several nnxyz pieces in the owned subset, where the collector sees shared raw mark-making across both artists.

connections.reason: Both show asymmetric eyes and bared teeth against a saturated background, but "nnotb #190" buries its features under denser scribble, making its face harder to read than "Wobbler"'s open layout.
Both use a row of vertical white teeth as a strong horizontal anchor, though "nifty faces #51" frames its mouth inside a rigid rectangular scaffold while "Wobbler" lets the jaw float loosely.
